decks.notes: The deck is focused on utilizing Paradoxical Outcome to generate massive card advantage and mana acceleration through artifacts like Grim Monolith and Mishra's Workshop. The key strategy is to quickly assemble a board state that allows for infinite mana generation or card draw, leading to a game-winning combo fueled by The One Ring or Urza's Saga. By efficiently cycling through the deck with cards like Sensei's Divining Top and Mystic Forge, the deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with powerful plays and combos early in the game.

This deck focuses on using Oath of Druids to cheat powerful creatures into play, such as Atraxa, Grand Unifier. It also utilizes control elements like Force of Will and Oko, Thief of Crowns to disrupt the opponent's game plan. The inclusion of Show and Tell allows for additional ways to cheat creatures into play. The deck also features powerful card draw and selection with cards like Ancestral Recall and Brainstorm, as well as tutors like Demonic Tutor and Vampiric Tutor to find key pieces. Additionally, the deck includes disruption with cards like Thoughtseize and Karn, the Great Creator.

The deck focuses on using fast mana acceleration and powerful spells to assemble a combo win condition. The main strategy involves using cards like Tinker and Demonic Tutor to find key pieces like Goblin Charbelcher or Thassa's Oracle, while also disrupting the opponent with counterspells like Force of Will and Pact of Negation. The combo finish involves milling the deck with cards like Balustrade Spy and Undercity Informer to win the game in one explosive turn. The deck aims to quickly assemble its combo pieces and win the game before the opponent can establish their own game plan.

The key concept of this deck is to quickly assemble the combo pieces, primarily Coveted Jewel, using powerful mana acceleration like Mishra's Workshop and mana rocks like the Moxen. The deck aims to generate advantage through card draw and manipulation with cards like Ancestral Recall and Paradoxical Outcome, while also disrupting the opponent's plans with counter spells like Force of Will. The ultimate goal is to lock the opponent out of the game with cards like Trinisphere and control the game with powerful artifacts like Mystic Forge and The One Ring.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's game plan through countermagic and removal spells, while also leveraging powerful card draw and tutor effects to assemble key combo pieces like Time Vault and Vexing Bauble with Manifold Key. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value by allowing for additional card recursion and flexibility in the late game. Overall, the deck aims to control the game and outmaneuver the opponent to secure victory.

The deck is centered around disrupting opponents with hatebear creatures that prevent them from playing multiple spells per turn or casting noncreature spells efficiently. This aggressive strategy is supported by ramp and mana acceleration from fast mana artifacts, allowing for quick deployment of disruptive creatures and efficient use of resources. The inclusion of hand disruption and targeted removal in the form of March of Otherworldly Light and Strip Mine further adds to the deck's ability to disrupt opponents while maintaining pressure on the battlefield.

The primary strategy of this deck is to control the game through counterspells and disruption while utilizing Oath of Druids to cheat powerful creatures into play. The deck aims to quickly ramp up its mana with fast mana sources like Black Lotus and the Moxen, allowing it to cast big threats like Atraxa, Grand Unifier or Bolas's Citadel. Show and Tell and Tinker can also be used to put game-winning threats into play. The deck has a strong control element with cards like Force of Will and Thoughtseize to disrupt the opponent's game plan.

The main focus of this deck is to control the game through powerful spells and abilities while utilizing the Oath of Druids card to cheat out powerful creatures like Atraxa, Grand Unifier. The deck includes a combination of powerful counterspells, card draw, and tutors to help find key cards like Show and Tell and Tinker to create advantageous board states. Additionally, the inclusion of cards like Bolas's Citadel and Oko, Thief of Crowns provide additional value and utility to strengthen the deck's control capabilities.

This deck focuses on early aggressive plays with hatebears to disrupt the opponent's strategy. By deploying disruptive creatures like Chancellor of the Annex and Archon of Emeria, combined with efficient mana acceleration from Moxen and other artifacts, the deck aims to pressure the opponent while limiting their options. The inclusion of cards like White Plume Adventurer and Witch Enchanter provide additional value and card advantage. With a mix of disruptive creatures and powerful artifacts, this deck aims to control the game and secure victory through early aggression and disruption.

The core strategy of this deck revolves around assembling and resolving the Doomsday combo, utilizing cards like Dark Ritual, Demonic Tutor, and Force of Will to set up and protect the win condition. By manipulating the top cards of the library and using Thassa's Oracle or Undercity Sewers as the finisher, the deck aims to win the game in a single explosive turn. The inclusion of powerful draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time helps to dig deeper into the deck and find the necessary pieces for the combo.

The deck focuses on quickly assembling a winning combination of cards, primarily centered around the Doomsday spell. By efficiently cycling through the deck and manipulating the top cards, the deck aims to set up a situation where casting Doomsday will result in victory. It includes key cards like Thassa's Oracle and Demonic Consultation to win the game on the spot. The deck is designed to be fast and ruthless, aiming to execute its game plan before opponents have a chance to respond effectively.

The core theme of this deck is to overwhelm the opponent with efficient creatures and disruptive spells, while also utilizing hate cards to slow down opposing strategies. By deploying powerful creatures like Archon of Emeria and White Plume Adventurer, and disrupting the opponent's game plan with Chancellor of the Annex and Anointed Peacekeeper, this deck aims to establish a strong board presence while denying the opponent's resources. Additionally, the deck uses efficient mana acceleration from artifacts, land destruction with Strip Mine and Wasteland, and protection from counterspells with Cavern of Souls to maintain tempo and pressure the opponent.

This deck focuses on using powerful control spells to disrupt the opponent's game plan while gaining card advantage through cantrips and card draw. The goal is to control the tempo of the game until the player can establish a strong board presence with creatures like Deathrite Shaman and Lórien Revealed. The deck also utilizes powerful mana acceleration from artifact mana sources like Black Lotus and the Moxen to quickly deploy threats and protect them with counterspells like Force of Will and Spell Pierce. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value by allowing the player to recur low-cost permanents from the graveyard.

The focus of this deck revolves around utilizing Oath of Druids as a win condition, alongside Show and Tell to cheat in powerful creatures like Atraxa, Grand Unifier and Oko, Thief of Crowns. The deck also includes a mix of control elements such as Force of Will and Mental Misstep to disrupt the opponent's game plan. Additionally, there are card draw spells like Brainstorm and Dig Through Time to ensure consistent access to key pieces. The inclusion of mana acceleration with Moxen and fetch lands helps to ramp up quickly and cast spells efficiently.

This deck focuses on assembling the Coveted Jewel combo, using powerful artifacts like Tolarian Academy, Grim Monolith, and Mana Crypt to generate mana quickly. It also includes cards like Paradoxical Outcome and Mishra's Workshop to draw cards and dig for key pieces. The deck aims to quickly ramp up and control the game, ultimately winning through the combo of Coveted Jewel, Time Vault, and The One Ring to create a powerful advantage over the opponent. The deck has strong artifact synergy and uses powerful interaction like Force of Will to protect its game plan.

This Dimir Control deck aims to disrupt the opponent's strategy while efficiently controlling the game. It utilizes powerful card draw and tutoring effects like Ancestral Recall, Demonic Tutor, and Dig Through Time to ensure card advantage. The deck also includes disruptive spells like Drown in the Loch, Force of Will, and Flusterstorm to control the opponent's spells. Lurrus of the Dream-Den provides additional value by allowing the player to recur creatures from the graveyard. Overall, this deck focuses on maintaining control of the game through card advantage and disruption.
